stories.label: Iran in Port Sudan? The Next Threat to Asian Markets
stories.summary: The Red Sea has two shores, and this file — like almost everyone — has covered only the Yemeni one. Lead with the asymmetry: Bab el-Mandeb traffic is priced off Houthi risk, while the western shore is a state in its fourth year of civil war whose de facto capital, Port Sudan, is the single point through which Sudan's trade, aid and oil transit route all pass, and Iran has been supplying and courting the army that holds it. Teach the mechanism our reader can apply: a chokepoint is only as secure as its weakest coastline, because anti-ship weapons need range and a launch point, not a navy — so a foothold on the Sudanese coast would put the corridor under threat from two directions at once, and the insurers who set the premium for every Asian-bound cargo do not distinguish between the shores. Establish the record: what Iranian involvement in Sudan is actually documented (drone transfers to the SAF, port and naval-access discussions and their status) versus what is inferred, who controls Port Sudan today and the RSF's reach against it, the volume of Asia-bound trade through Bab el-Mandeb and current transit counts against baseline, and what Khartoum, Tehran and the Gulf states each say. Then the frame this file should press: Sudan's war is covered, when it is covered, as a humanitarian catastrophe with no strategic dimension — and that framing is exactly why nobody is watching the coastline that could reprice half the world's freight. Fills the Africa gap the audit has now flagged five days running. Analysis piece from a specialist outlet: take the documented transfers and the traffic numbers, treat the forward-looking claim as a hypothesis and label it one. SOURCING NOTE: Sudan is an OIC member and the feed carries no Sudanese or regional outlet — seek Radio Dabanga, Sudan Tribune or Al Jazeera at the writing stage; log as a feed-side gap.

stories.label: Unsupervised dietary-behavioral profiling identifies PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) and metal exposure patterns in Korean adults
stories.summary: The study asks not what Korean adults eat but how they eat — packaged, prepared, takeaway, home-cooked — and finds that the behavioural pattern, not the food itself, predicts who carries the highest burden of PFAS and heavy metals. Lead with that inversion, because it is what makes the finding actionable and unsettling at once: exposure tracks packaging and preparation, so the contamination is coming from the container and the process rather than from the diet a nutritionist would assess. Teach the mechanism: PFAS are used for grease and water resistance in food packaging and non-stick surfaces and migrate into the food they touch, and they are called forever chemicals because the carbon-fluorine bond does not break down in the environment or in the body — so a dietary-behaviour cluster is really a packaging-exposure cluster, and the people in it are the ones who eat convenience food because they have least time, not least care. Establish the record: cohort size and design, which clusters the unsupervised method produced and how they were characterised, which PFAS congeners and which metals were measured and at what concentrations against national reference values, effect sizes rather than significance alone, and what the authors state as limits — and note this is an unedited early-access manuscript. Then the frame our reader should carry: PFAS regulation is being written in the EU and the US on the basis of Western exposure data, while the packaging industry sells globally — a Korean cohort finding that behaviour beats diet as a predictor is directly transferable to Gulf, Malaysian, Turkish and Indonesian populations whose packaged-food consumption is rising fastest and whose regulators have no equivalent biomonitoring programme to detect it.

stories.label: Indigenous-led conservation helps save endangered cockatoo
stories.summary: An Indonesian community has stabilised one of the world's rarest cockatoos without giving up the centuries-old sacred practice that involves the bird — and the research documenting it was led jointly by an Australian university, Universitas Gadjah Mada and an Indonesian conservation body. Lead with the design, not the outcome: the intervention worked because it treated the tradition as a constraint to build around rather than a problem to remove. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry, because it overturns the default model: conventional conservation converts habitat into protected area and local users into trespassers, which produces enforcement costs, resentment and poaching by the people who know the forest best — whereas an arrangement that keeps the community as the custodian converts the same people into the monitoring network, and monitoring is the expensive part. Establish the record: which cockatoo species and its population trajectory and IUCN status, what the sacred practice actually is and how the arrangement accommodates it, what the Journal of Ethnobiology paper measured and over what period, the trapping and trade pressure the species faces including CITES status, who funds the arrangement and what happens when the funding ends, and what the researchers state as limits. Then the frame: Indonesia is the world's most biodiverse archipelago and the largest Muslim-majority country, and its conservation is routinely reported as a story about what foreign NGOs do there — this is a case where the community is the actor and the outsiders are the recorders, which is the correct relation and the rarer one. SOURCING NOTE: Indonesia is an OIC member and the feed carries no Indonesian outlet — seek Jakarta Post or Mongabay Indonesia at the writing stage; log as a feed-side gap.

stories.label: Bending Spoons to buy Airtable for $1.28B
stories.summary: Airtable, valued at $11bn in 2021, is being bought by Bending Spoons — the Italian firm that already owns Evernote, WeTransfer, Vimeo and AOL — at a fraction of that peak. Lead with the markdown and with the acquirer's catalogue, because together they describe a business model our reader will now start seeing everywhere: buying software with a large installed base and no growth, cutting engineering and support hard, and raising prices on users who cannot easily leave. Teach the mechanism, because it is the part that matters to anyone whose team or company depends on a SaaS tool: switching cost is the asset being purchased — data locked in a proprietary schema, workflows built by people who have left, integrations nobody wants to rebuild — so the acquisition is a bet on how much price a captive base absorbs before it moves, and Evernote's post-acquisition price rises and staff cuts are the published precedent. Establish the record: the equity value and the enterprise value and why the reported figures differ, the 2021 valuation and what Airtable's revenue and headcount are now, what Bending Spoons did to each prior acquisition and on what timeline, what both companies say about continuity of service and pricing, and how the deal is financed. Then the frame our reader should act on: the software small businesses, universities and NGOs across South Asia, Africa and the Gulf run on is increasingly owned by consolidators whose returns come from raising rents on locked-in data — the practical question is what your own exit path from a tool looks like, and whether the export button still works. Two carriers, Bloomberg and TechCrunch, divergence 0.02 — note the headline figures disagree and reconcile them explicitly.

stories.label: Digi Yatra: Aadhaar, Driving Licence for Contactless Airport Entry
stories.summary: India's face-recognition airport entry system now accepts a driving licence through DigiLocker as well as Aadhaar. Lead with what the expansion is actually for, because it is not convenience: broadening the accepted credential removes the last practical reason a traveller had to stay outside the system, and a scheme with no non-biometric alternative at the gate stops being voluntary regardless of what the policy says. Teach the mechanism our reader should carry into every national digital-ID rollout: Digi Yatra's stated design is decentralised — the face template is held on the passenger's phone and matched at the airport, with deletion promised after the flight — and the entire privacy case rests on that architecture being implemented and audited as described, by a private-sector foundation that is not a public authority and is not subject to the transparency obligations of one. Establish the record: how enrolment and verification actually work and where the biometric is stored at each step, which airports are live and how many passengers are enrolled, what the retention and deletion policy states and who verifies it, whether a non-Digi-Yatra queue is guaranteed and staffed, who governs the Digi Yatra Foundation and its data-sharing terms, and what India's data protection act obliges here. Then the frame: this is the template being exported — Aadhaar-derived identity stacks are being sold or gifted to Indonesia, Nigeria, Bangladesh, Morocco and the Gulf, and the design decision our reader should judge is not whether biometric boarding works but whether the opt-out survives contact with a system that makes every other queue slower.

stories.label: The global grassroots gatherings trying to humanize the AI boom
stories.summary: Local AI salons in Nairobi, Indian cities and the US are where practitioners outside the labs are working out what the technology is for — and the reporting is candid that these rooms are largely English-speaking, laptop-owning and urban. Lead with that tension rather than with the warm version, because it is the finding: the venues built to widen the conversation reproduce the filter they were meant to remove. Teach the mechanism our reader should recognise, and connect it to what this file reported yesterday on open-weight models and export controls — a model you can download is only accessible if you also have the hardware to run it, the bandwidth to fetch it, the English to read its documentation and the free evenings to learn it, so 'open' distributes capability along the lines of existing privilege unless something deliberately counteracts that. The salons are the counteraction, and their limits are the measure of how much is needed. Establish the record: which groups, in which cities, who convenes and funds them, what they actually do, how large they are, what the participants say they get, and which languages and audiences they reach and miss. Then the frame this file should press: Kenya, Nigeria, Pakistan and Indonesia are being told they can build on open models rather than buy from closed ones, and the binding constraint is not licence terms but the depth of the local practitioner base — which is grown in rooms like these, or not at all. Rest of World reporting from the places the AI story is usually told about rather than from; keep the scepticism the piece itself carries.

stories.label: MaiaSpace Losses Required ArianeGroup to Decide on Company's Future
stories.summary: Europe's answer to the Falcon 9 posted a €37.5m loss and drove its shareholders' equity below zero, which under French company law forces the parent to formally decide whether to dissolve it — ArianeGroup said no. Lead with that legal trigger, because it is a fact from a filed account rather than a press release, and it dates the moment Europe's reusable-rocket programme became a decision someone had to sign. Teach the mechanism our reader can use on any state-adjacent champion: negative equity with €114.2m still in the bank is not insolvency, it is accumulated development spend exceeding paid-in capital — normal for a launch startup and fatal for one whose shareholder is an incumbent that profits from the expendable rocket the new vehicle is meant to replace. That conflict, not the engineering, is the risk. Establish the record: the 2025 accounts as filed on 22 July 2026, cash position against burn rate, Maia's stated first-flight date and how it has moved, what ArianeGroup decided and what recapitalisation it implies, Ariane 6's flight rate and per-launch cost against Falcon 9's, and what the company says. Then the frame: launch access is sovereignty — the countries this file writes for buy their satellite launches from someone, and the practical shortlist has narrowed to SpaceX, China and India while Europe spends a decade deciding. Turkey, the UAE, Indonesia and Pakistan all have national satellite programmes and none has a domestic ride; every year Europe fails to field a reusable vehicle is a year the terms are set by two governments. MULTI-SOURCE NOTE: this is a niche pick because the feed supplied no usable multi-source economy story — see the note on this cycle's floors.

stories.label: Aramco's profits soar 44 percent as Iran war boosts prices
stories.summary: Lead with the number and who booked it: Aramco's quarterly profit rose 44 percent because the war that closed shipping lanes raised the price of every barrel it still ships — and its CEO told reporters the Houthi strikes had 'no material impact on our capabilities'. The mechanism our reader should carry: a war-risk premium is not a cost to a producer with intact export infrastructure, it is revenue, because the premium is priced into the barrel while Aramco's lifting cost is unchanged — so the same disruption that our Hormuz filings showed as a permanent tax on Pakistani, Egyptian and Bangladeshi importers lands on this balance sheet as a windfall. Establish the record: Q2 profit and the year-ago comparison, average realised price, production and export volumes against the pre-escalation baseline, what damage the July attacks actually did, the dividend and how much of it goes to the Saudi state budget, and what Nasser said versus what the filings show. Then the frame: the ummah does not experience this war as one economy — the producer states are being paid by the disruption that is impoverishing the importer states, and that divergence is the most consequential thing happening inside the OIC right now. Four carriers across Egypt, the US, the Gulf and the Arab press, divergence 0.13 — note that Bloomberg leads on operational reassurance while Ahram and The New Arab lead on the profit itself, and attribute each framing.

stories.label: The coffins come free here with the story
stories.summary: A reporter in Kalat was told that if he is new to journalism he might need a coffin, and to say so in advance so one could be sent. Lead with that sentence and with who is affected: the handful of stringers who are the only people reporting from Balochistan, Pakistan's largest province by area and its least covered by anyone. The mechanism to teach: a beat does not go dark by censorship order, it goes dark by attrition — anonymous calls, disappearances, and the absence of any employer willing to name the caller mean the cost of filing is borne entirely by the individual, so the province produces no record and the absence of a record is then read as the absence of events. That is why insurgency, military operations and enforced disappearances in Balochistan reach our reader only as a casualty figure from Islamabad. Establish the record: what the threats were and to whom, how many Baloch journalists have been killed or disappeared and over what period, what press bodies and the provincial government say, and what the reporter was working on. Then the frame: the ummah's own information about its own peripheries is produced by people who are being told to expect coffins, and every wire story datelined Quetta rests on them. Regional outlet on a regional story, doing the reporting no one else will — single-source ground account, so attribute the threats as reported and state what is uncorroborated.

stories.label: EXCLUSIVE: This is how former Gov. Sylva's alleged coup donations were shared
stories.summary: Premium Times traces how money allegedly given by a former Bayelsa State governor to last year's failed coup against Tinubu was disbursed among the suspected plotters. Lead with the disbursement trail rather than the plot, because the trail is the new fact and it is what makes a coup attempt legible: coups are usually reported as an event, and this reporting treats one as a financed transaction with named recipients and amounts. Teach the mechanism our reader can apply across West Africa's coup belt: a garrison seizure needs cash before it needs soldiers — for allowances, movement and the first days of holding a capital — and the financiers are almost always civilian political losers rather than officers, which is why coup accountability so consistently stops at the rank of major. Establish the record: what documents or testimony Premium Times has, the amounts and the named recipients, Sylva's response and his counsel's, the status of the ongoing prosecutions and how many are in detention without charge, and what the presidency has said. Then the frame: Nigeria is Africa's largest economy and largest Muslim population, and the durability of its civilian order is the single biggest variable in the Sahel's next five years — a coup that failed still tells you the price of one. Fills the Africa gap the audit has flagged for four consecutive days; investigative Nigerian outlet doing original work, so the single-source exception applies squarely. Note the feed's concept tags for this entry are mis-resolved — ignore them.

stories.label: Drone strike kills at least 5 in Russia's Moscow region: Governor
stories.summary: Five killed and six wounded in Chekhov, in the Moscow region, by a Ukrainian long-range drone — a day after a drone struck a crowded beach at Gelendzhik. Lead with the dead and where they were, because dignity requires that Russian civilians killed by drones be counted and named to exactly the standard this file applies to Ukrainian civilians killed by missiles, and our recent filings have run one direction. Teach the mechanism: long-range strike drones are cheap, slow and numerous, so they are intercepted by air defence rather than avoided — which means casualties in defended areas are frequently caused by debris and by interceptors, and 'downed over the region' and 'no casualties' are claims that the same governor issues about the same night. Say who is claiming what. Establish the record: the strike location and time, the confirmed dead and wounded and whether they are named, what Russian air defence claims for the night, whether Kyiv has claimed the strike and what target it names, and the pattern of long-range strikes on civilian-adjacent infrastructure by both parties over the past week. Then the frame our reader should hold: four and a half years in, both militaries are prosecuting this war primarily against the other's rear, where the people are — and the reciprocity is the point, because it is what makes the war's end recede. Four carriers across Russia, Turkey, Iran and Azerbaijan, divergence 0.21 — RT is a party's state outlet, so attribute its characterisations to it and prefer Anadolu's and APA's counts where they differ; note Mehr's headline totals killed and injured together.

stories.label: Arbaeen Pilgrimage: World's largest peaceful gathering
stories.summary: Tens of millions of people are about to walk the fifty miles from Najaf to Karbala, and the reason our reader has probably never seen it reported at scale is the story's second half. Lead with the arithmetic — Arbaeen is by participant count the largest annual peaceful gathering on earth, several times the size of Hajj, and it is fed and housed almost entirely by mawakib, unpaid roadside stations run by Iraqi households along the route. Teach that mechanism, because it is genuinely remarkable and almost never described: this is a logistics operation of tens of millions of meals with no ministry, no ticketing and no corporate sponsor, and it runs annually in a country whose state cannot deliver electricity. Then the frame that makes this cycle's filing news rather than an explainer: this year the walk crosses an Iraq that is being struck — US and Saudi strikes on Iraqi militia targets, Baghdad calling them a violation of sovereignty, and border crossings carrying Iranian pilgrims into a country at the centre of a regional war. Establish the record: this year's registered and estimated pilgrim numbers against last year's, what Iraqi and Iranian authorities have announced on the Mehran and Shalamcheh crossings and on security, any casualty or crowd incidents, and what the war has done to the route. Report a Shia devotional practice with precision and respect and without either sectarian framing or state-media triumphalism — Mehr is an Iranian state outlet and the framing must be attributed. Seek an Iraqi outlet at the writing stage; the feed carries none.

stories.label: India: Dhaka presses Delhi on stance ahead of Hasina speech
stories.summary: Bangladesh has asked India to state its position before Sheikh Hasina — ousted, convicted in absentia, and sheltered in India — delivers a 'homecoming' speech tomorrow. Lead with the demand and with what makes it unusual: a government is asking a neighbour to declare in advance whether it will let a deposed leader address the country she fled, which is a sovereignty question dressed as a scheduling question. Teach the mechanism our reader can use on every exile politics story: asylum for a former head of government is not a neutral humanitarian act once the exile broadcasts — hosting becomes a platform, and a platform is a policy, so Delhi's silence is itself the answer Dhaka is objecting to. India has no extradition route it is willing to use and Bangladesh has no leverage beyond the relationship itself. Establish the record: what State Minister Shama Obaed Islam actually said, the status of Hasina's convictions and Dhaka's extradition request under the 2013 treaty and India's stated grounds for not acting, what India's ministry has said, where the speech will be delivered and to whom, and where Bangladesh's own election timetable stands. Then the frame: two years after the uprising, the interim order's central unfinished business is accountability for the killings of protesters, and that case cannot close while the defendant is a guest of the region's largest power. SOURCING NOTE: Bangladesh is an OIC member and the feed carries only a German outlet on this — seek Prothom Alo, The Daily Star or Dhaka Tribune at the writing stage and log as a feed-side gap.

stories.label: Japan's Toyota reports hefty profit on cheap yen and solid car sales
stories.summary: Toyota's quarterly profit nearly doubled to 1.48 trillion yen, and the largest single reason is not a car — it is the exchange rate. Lead with how much of the gain is translation rather than trade, because that is the mechanism our reader should carry out of every Japanese earnings season: an exporter books revenue in dollars and costs in yen, so a weak yen inflates profit without a single extra unit sold, and the same weak yen raises the price of every barrel, tonne of wheat and imported component the domestic economy buys. Toyota's shareholders and Japanese households are on opposite sides of the same number. Establish the record: the profit figure and the year-ago comparison, the assumed exchange rate and the disclosed currency contribution, unit sales by region with the US and India called out, what tariffs and the Hormuz-driven energy and freight costs did to the cost line, and Toyota's own guidance. Then the frame this file should press: the yen's level is not a market outcome alone — our recent filing covered US support for the currency, and a managed exchange rate is an industrial subsidy paid by importers, which matters to every South and Southeast Asian market where Toyota competes against cheaper Chinese EVs whose own currency is managed the same way. Two US carriers, divergence 0 — go to the company's filed statement rather than the wire summary.

stories.label: Bhutan's Gelephu Mindfulness City puts part of its BTC treasury to work after 10,000 bitcoin pledge
stories.summary: A special administrative region inside Bhutan has handed part of a 10,000-bitcoin sovereign treasury to an outside asset manager and says the mandate is meant to create jobs for Bhutanese youth. Lead with the size of the holding relative to the country, because that ratio is the story: a state whose entire economy is a few billion dollars is holding a reserve asset that can move twenty percent in a month, and it got there by mining with hydropower it could otherwise export. Teach the mechanism our reader should weigh honestly: a sovereign wealth fund exists to convert a depleting or volatile resource into a stable income stream, and putting that fund into the most volatile liquid asset in the world inverts the purpose — unless the bet is precisely that a small landlocked country cannot access conventional capital markets on decent terms and has chosen an asset no creditor can sanction. Both readings are defensible; give the numbers and let the reader judge. Establish the record: the size and cost basis of the holding, what the 3iQ mandate actually permits, who bears the drawdown risk, how the coins were mined and at what electricity opportunity cost, Gelephu's legal status and who governs its treasury, and what officials and the manager say versus what is contractually committed. Then the frame: Gulf and Central Asian states are watching this as a template for monetising stranded energy, and the jobs promise is the part with no disclosed detail — say so.

stories.label: US Northwest battles wildfires after Spokane neighborhoods scorched
stories.summary: Sixty-five thousand people evacuated and hundreds of buildings burned inside a US city of a quarter of a million. Lead with the evacuation number and the word 'neighbourhoods', because the finding is that this is not a forest fire that reached a town — it is an urban conflagration, and the fuel was the houses. Teach the mechanism precisely, since it now governs fire risk from California to Athens to Cape Town: under drought and extreme heat, embers travel a kilometre or more ahead of the front, and once one structure ignites, the dominant fuel becomes the built environment itself, so suppression stops being firefighting and becomes evacuation logistics. That is why the defensible-space rules that work for isolated homes fail at neighbourhood density. Establish the record: the acreage and containment, the confirmed dead and injured, structures destroyed and how many are homes, the temperature and drought indices for the Inland Northwest against the historical range, the evacuation order timeline, and what the state and federal agencies say about resources. Then the frame our reader should carry to a hotter world's less-resourced cities: the same week Europe's rivers ran too low to cool a reactor, an American city with the world's best-funded fire service lost neighbourhoods anyway — and Lahore, Karachi, Cairo and Lagos face the same heat with none of that capacity and far denser informal housing. Wire copy relayed by a science aggregator; go to the incident command's own figures rather than the summary.

stories.label: Evaluation of perimenstrual atopy in apparently healthy females through hormonal, immune, and autonomic changes across menstrual phases: a prospective study
stories.summary: A prospective study finds measurable allergic sensitisation in healthy women that rises and falls with the menstrual cycle, tracked simultaneously through hormones, immune markers and autonomic function. Lead with the fact that these were healthy volunteers, not patients, because that is what makes the finding structural: if atopy is cyclical in people with no diagnosis, then every asthma, eczema and allergy measurement taken from a woman is a single point on a curve nobody was controlling for. Teach the mechanism the paper is testing: oestrogen and progesterone act directly on mast cells and on the autonomic balance that sets airway tone, so the same allergen dose can produce different responses in the same person two weeks apart — which is a plausible physiological reason, not a behavioural one, for why women's symptom reports have historically been read as inconsistent. Establish the record: the cohort size and design, which phases were sampled and how often, which hormonal, immune and autonomic measures moved and by how much, effect sizes and confidence intervals rather than significance alone, and what the authors state as limits. Note this is an unedited early-access manuscript and say so. Then the frame: clinical trials only began routinely enrolling women of reproductive age in the 1990s and still rarely stratify by cycle phase, so a mechanism this basic being newly quantified in 2026 is itself the accountability finding — and the reader most affected is the woman whose inhaler dose was titrated on a bad week.

stories.label: Xi Jinping's AI Vision
stories.summary: Xi addressed the World Artificial Intelligence Conference, and the audience was not in the room — it was every state that has been told by Washington which chips and now which robots it may buy. Lead with what China is actually offering, in institutional terms: a proposed global AI governance body and open-weight models released free, set directly against an American regime of export controls and, as this file reported yesterday, an FTC order closing the US market to foreign humanoids. Teach the mechanism our reader should apply rather than the rhetoric: open weights are a strategy, not a gift — a model you can download and run on your own hardware creates a developer base, a toolchain and a dependency that no export control can revoke, which is exactly how a standard is captured, and it is the same play that made Android the phone operating system of the Global South. Establish the record: what Xi specifically proposed and what institutional form it would take, which Chinese models are open-weight and under what licence, what the US export control and market-access measures currently prohibit, who attended and who did not, and what Chinese and US officials each say. Then the frame that matters to this file's readers: Indonesia, Turkey, the Gulf, Pakistan and Nigeria are being asked to choose a stack, and the cheaper open one comes with a governance framework written in Beijing while the expensive closed one comes with a licence Washington can revoke — neither is sovereignty, and pretending there is a third option is the thing to avoid. Analysis piece — take the speech text and the verifiable measures, not the framing.

stories.label: Why the Legendary Erdős Problems Are Falling to AI
stories.summary: This file reported the announcement that AI systems had settled ten longstanding maths problems; Quanta reports why those problems and not others, which is the part that tells you what was actually demonstrated. Advance the arc, do not restate it. Lead with the property mathematicians are pointing to: Erdős problems are typically short to state, combinatorial, self-contained, and solvable by a clever bounded construction rather than by building new theory — so they are close to the ideal case for a system that searches a huge space of candidate arguments and can verify each one cheaply. Teach that as the mechanism, because it generalises: automated success tracks verifiability and problem compactness, not difficulty, which is why a problem humans found hard for sixty years can fall while a routine step in a research programme does not. Establish the record: which problems were resolved and by which systems, whether the proofs were machine-verified and by whom, what working mathematicians quoted here say the results do and do not show, how many Erdős problems remain open, and where the same approach has failed. Then the frame our reader will want: the interesting question is not whether AI does mathematics but which parts of intellectual work have this shape — cheap to check, expensive to find — because those are the parts being automated first everywhere, from proof to code review to drug screening. Specialist outlet doing the analysis no wire did; keep the distinction between 'solved' and 'verified' explicit throughout.

stories.label: BTC news: A bitcoin wallet dormant since 2013 moved $31 million
stories.summary: A wallet untouched since 2013 moved $31 million on Monday, and it was not alone — a spike in decade-old coins moving on-chain, in the middle of the Coldcard firmware compromise this file covered yesterday. Lead with the ambiguity, because the ambiguity is the finding and it is technically instructive: an on-chain observer cannot distinguish a thief consolidating stolen coins from a frightened long-term holder sweeping to a new device, since both produce the same transaction shape. Advance the arc with the new fact — the movement spike and the fourth sweep — rather than restating the vulnerability. Teach the mechanism our reader can carry: bitcoin's ledger is fully public and fully pseudonymous, so the network offers total visibility of what moved and no information about who moved it or why, and the entire forensic industry that reads it is inference dressed as data. Establish the record: the specific transactions and their sizes, how the dormancy figures were derived and by whom, the running total attributed to the Coldcard sweeps, what the vendor has said since destroying inventory, and which claims come from on-chain analytics firms with a product to sell. Then the frame: self-custody moves trust rather than removing it, and the people who bear a firmware failure hardest are not speculators but the users in Nigeria, Turkey, Lebanon and Argentina who hold coins because their bank or currency already failed them — with no issuer, no insurance and no reversal. Do not assert attribution the chain cannot support.

stories.label: Zelenskyy sacks Ukraine's US ambassador
stories.summary: Ukraine's ambassador to Washington — its single most consequential diplomatic post — is dismissed by presidential decree while under investigation by the country's own anti-corruption bureau, without being formally accused of anything. Lead with that sequence, because it is the mechanism: a decree requires no charge, no finding and no appeal, so the removal happens on the president's timetable and the investigation on NABU's, and the public cannot tell which drove which. Teach our reader what NABU is and why it matters far beyond Ukraine: it is an independent anti-corruption agency built at Western insistence as a condition of aid, and every attempt to bring it back under presidential control since 2015 has triggered a domestic and donor backlash — so an investigation touching a presidential appointee is a test of exactly the institution the money was meant to build. Establish the record: who Olga Stefanishyna is and what she was appointed to do, what NABU has and has not said, what the decree states, who replaces her, and the Mindich case that RT foregrounds and the others do not. Then the frame: wartime states concentrate power for reasons everyone accepts, and the accountability machinery is always the first thing the concentration reaches. Three carriers across Turkey, Hong Kong and Russia, divergence 0.31 — RT reads this as corruption, TRT and SCMP as personnel; attribute every characterisation to the outlet making it and go to the decree text.

stories.label: Shipping traffic at key Gulf waterways little changed on uncertain peace talks
stories.summary: Twenty vessels — 12 tankers and eight others — transited on the first day of the week, and that number is the story: it is essentially unchanged, which contradicts both of the competing claims this file reported yesterday. Lead with the AIS count against the rhetoric, because our Hormuz arc has spent three filings on a source-symmetry problem (Washington says it fully controls the strait and that Iran agreed to talks; Tehran says there are no US negotiations, only Omani mediation) and vessel-tracking data is the first evidence in the arc that neither side controls. Teach the mechanism our reader can carry: a strait is not closed or open, it is priced — the war-risk premium, the insurers' listed area, and the escort queue are what actually ration transits, so traffic holding flat while diplomacy is 'ambiguous' means the market has priced neither a settlement nor a closure, and shipowners are the only party here with money on the answer. Establish the record: the counts for Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz against the pre-escalation baseline, the war-risk premium level, WTI and Brent on the day, what each government has said in the last 48 hours, and what the shipping-data provider actually measures. Then the frame: the people who bear this are not traders but the importers downstream — Pakistan, Egypt, Bangladesh and the East African coast buy energy and wheat through these two chokepoints, and a premium that never lifts is a permanent tax on food and fuel in countries that had no part in the war. Third and final filing permitted on this arc — after this, the arc rests unless the transit numbers themselves move. SOURCING NOTE: primary affected region is the Gulf (multiple OIC members) and the cluster carries only Reuters and Times of Israel; the feed offers no Gulf or Iranian outlet on this specific data story. Seek Arab News, The National or Tehran Times at the writing stage and log as a feed-side gap.

stories.label: Fear, Loss, and Hope Amid Israel's War on South Lebanon
stories.summary: Residents of south Lebanon describing an onslaught that has no end date and, increasingly, no expectation of one — the fear named in the reporting is not of the next strike but of prolonged occupation. Lead with the residents and what they say, because this file has covered Gaza, Hormuz and the Patriot supply chain without once reaching the third front, and the people living under it are the only source here. Teach the mechanism our reader should hold: the November 2024 cessation-of-hostilities arrangement was not a peace treaty and did not require withdrawal on any enforceable schedule — it created five 'points' Israeli forces retained pending conditions that only one party certifies, and a temporary position held past its stated purpose is how every long occupation in this region began. That is why the residents' fear is a structural reading and not a mood. Establish the record: which villages and how many people remain displaced, the number of strikes and named dead since the cessation began, what the arrangement's text actually obliges and by when, the positions still held and what Israel, the Lebanese state and UNIFIL each say about them, and the state of reconstruction funding for the south. Then the frame our reader will want: Lebanon has no functioning central capacity to rebuild — the banking collapse of 2019 is still unresolved — so displacement here converts directly into permanent depopulation of the border belt, which is the outcome an occupation would otherwise have to achieve by force. Dignity requires the Lebanese dead be counted and named to the same standard this file applies in Gaza. Single-source ground report, not a Washington claim — attribute the residents' accounts as residents' accounts and note what is uncorroborated. SOURCING NOTE: Lebanon is an OIC member and the feed carries no Lebanese or regional outlet on this — seek L'Orient Today, Al Jazeera or The New Arab at the writing stage; log as a feed-side gap.

stories.label: Peshawar High Court upholds abolition of free electricity for officials of Wapda, Discos
stories.summary: A bench of two judges rejected the petitions of the men who run Pakistan's electricity system against losing the free electricity they gave themselves. Lead with the perk itself and its scale in units, because it is the cleanest available illustration of a phenomenon our reader hears about only as an abstraction: Pakistan's 'circular debt' is not a mystery of macroeconomics, it is an itemisable list of power delivered and never paid for, and the people who administer the billing were on that list. Teach the mechanism precisely: a distribution company recovers its costs from tariff, so every unit consumed off-book is recovered from the units that are billed — the perk was never free, it was a transfer from every household that pays, in a country where load-shedding rations power by the hour and the tariff has risen under IMF conditionality specifically to close this gap. Monetisation matters because it converts an invisible transfer into a visible line on a payslip that can be taxed, budgeted and cut. Establish the record: what the court actually held and on what grounds, how many officers across Wapda and which Discos, the estimated annual value of the units, where this sits in the IMF programme's structural benchmarks, the current circular-debt stock, and what the petitioners argued. Then the frame our reader will recognise across the region: elite in-kind privileges — free power, free fuel, free housing — survive austerity because they never appear as expenditure, and they are dismantled by courts and creditors rather than by parliaments, which tells you where accountability actually lives. Pairs with this cycle's petroleum-levy filing: both are the same question of who pays for the state's energy arithmetic in Pakistan, seen from the top and from the street.

stories.label: How a community-led campaign is helping save Nigeria's Kam language
stories.summary: Between 8,000 and 11,000 people speak Kam, and before 2016 no researcher had ever written it down. Lead with that second fact rather than the first, because it is the accountability finding: a language is not lost when its speakers die, it is lost when no institution ever considered it worth recording, and northeastern Nigeria has hundreds in that condition. Teach the mechanism our reader can carry: language death is a downstream effect of displacement and schooling policy, not of speaker preference — when a community is scattered by insecurity the intergenerational chain breaks in one generation, and when the only language of instruction and administration is English or Hausa, parents rationally stop transmitting the third. This is the same northeast whose displacement this file covered through Boko Haram's command structure two days ago; the language loss is the same event measured on a longer clock. Establish the record: what the campaign actually does (orthography, primers, recordings, who funds it), Kam's classification and speaker estimate and how it was arrived at, Nigeria's total language count and how many are rated endangered, what the national language-in-education policy provides on paper versus in practice, and what the campaigners themselves say they need. Then the frame: this is a community doing for itself the documentation a state and a university system did not do, and our reader should note who ends up holding the archive — because the ummah's linguistic inheritance across the Sahel is in the same position, and Arabic-script manuscript traditions in the region were lost the same way. Fills the Africa gap our audit has flagged for three consecutive days; this is the only Africa-subject story in the entire feed this cycle. SOURCING NOTE: Nigeria is an OIC member and the feed carries no Nigerian outlet on this — seek Premium Times, Daily Trust or Vanguard at the writing stage.

stories.label: JI claims govt collected Rs1.9 trillion through petroleum levy last year
stories.summary: Rs1.9 trillion taken at the pump in a single year, and a party is about to block the Indus Highway and the Bab-i-Khyber crossing on 7 August over it. Lead with the number and then with the constitutional detail that makes it the story: a petroleum levy is not a tax, it is a levy — so it sits outside the divisible pool that the National Finance Commission award splits with the provinces, and every rupee stays federal. That is why it grew: it is the one revenue instrument in Pakistan that does not have to be shared, does not require a new tax base, and can be raised by notification rather than by budget vote. Teach that mechanism, because our reader will recognise it everywhere — the fuel levy is the developing world's default emergency revenue, invisible in headline tax-to-GDP ratios, collected from people with no filing obligation, and structurally regressive since fuel is a larger share of a poor household's spending and passes into every freight and food price behind it. Establish the record: the levy rate per litre and how it moved over the year, the Rs1.9tn figure's provenance (this is Jamaat-i-Islami's claim — say so, and put it against the finance ministry's published collection), what the IMF programme requires on petroleum revenue, the ex-refinery versus retail price breakdown, and what the government says. Then the frame: a highway blockade is what politics looks like when a price rises without a vote — and the levy's whole design is that there is no vote to lose. Verify the claimed figure against official data rather than repeating the party's number; if it cannot be verified, attribute it and say what the official figure is. Regional outlet on a regional story, as it should be.

stories.label: Electric car to be charged using ethanol: Telangana launches India's first ethanol-powered EV charger
stories.summary: A charger that makes its own electricity from ethanol, so it needs no high-capacity grid connection, no transmission build and none of the approvals those require. Lead with what it removes rather than what it adds, because the binding constraint on EV adoption across South Asia and Africa was never the car — it is that a fast charger draws more power than the feeder on most streets can supply, and upgrading that feeder is a utility project with a multi-year queue. Teach the mechanism honestly and sceptically in the same breath: ethanol is reformed to hydrogen and run through a fuel cell, which is real chemistry and genuinely sidesteps the grid — but it also means the vehicle is now burning a crop, so the carbon case depends entirely on the feedstock, and the round-trip efficiency of ethanol → hydrogen → electricity → battery is far below simply plugging into a wire. Establish the record: who built it (Keto Motors), the unit's output and cost, the ethanol source and price per litre, what the E20 blending programme has already done to India's sugarcane and maize acreage and to fuel prices, and what the ministers actually announced versus what is operating. Then the frame our reader should hold: India is the world's test case for whether a country can electrify transport ahead of its grid, and the answer it is reaching for — distributed generation from biofuel — is one Pakistan, Nigeria, Indonesia and Egypt will read closely, because they have the same feeders and the same queue. Ask what the land and water cost of the ethanol is; single Indian business outlet on a government launch, so treat the announcement as an announcement.

stories.label: 'Mechanical shortcut' rapidly carries organic particles into the deep ocean
stories.summary: A physical process is moving organic carbon from the ocean surface to the seabed faster than the biological settling that climate models assume. Lead with what that does to the number rather than with the finding itself: the ocean's biological pump is the largest single carbon sink on the planet and the hardest to measure, so its efficiency is a parameter in every model that produces a carbon budget — and a budget is what every national climate pledge is subtracted from. Teach the mechanism our reader can hold: most carbon fixed by plankton at the surface is eaten and respired back before it sinks, so only a small fraction reaches depth, and the depth it reaches determines how long it stays down — decades at 200m, centuries below the thermocline. A mechanical shortcut that bypasses the slow settling changes both the fraction and the depth, which is why a measurement problem here propagates straight into policy arithmetic. Establish the record: what the shortcut physically is and where it was measured, the flux it accounts for against the previously assumed value, how the measurement spanned surface to deep ocean when that difficulty is the stated obstacle, the paper and journal, and what the authors state as limits and as unresolved. Then the frame our reader should carry, stated carefully and without overclaiming: a sink that is larger or faster than assumed is not good news to be banked — it is a revision to a term that was already the widest uncertainty in the budget, and the countries whose emissions allowances are computed from that budget are overwhelmingly not the ones running the ships that measure it. Pairs with this cycle's carbon-capture filing: one is the sink nature already runs, the other is the one industry proposes to build.

stories.label: Q&A: Does the world need 'carbon capture and storage' to reach net-zero?
stories.summary: An evidence synthesis of what carbon capture and storage has actually delivered against what every net-zero pathway assumes it will. Lead with the gap between deployed capacity and modelled capacity — the operating global total against the gigatonnes the scenarios require by 2050 — because that ratio is the whole argument and it is a measured number, not a projection. Teach the mechanism our reader needs to judge the technology on its merits: capture is thermodynamically expensive because CO2 in a flue stream is dilute, so the separation costs energy that must itself be generated, and the resulting parasitic load is why a captured plant burns more fuel per unit delivered — CCS is therefore genuinely necessary for the emissions that have no substitute (cement clinker chemistry, some steel) and genuinely marginal for power generation, where building the renewable is cheaper than capturing the coal. Establish the record: operating capacity and the share that goes to enhanced oil recovery rather than storage, cost per tonne across sectors, what the IPCC pathways assume and what happens to them at lower CCS deployment, storage-integrity and leakage evidence, and where the projects that failed failed. Then the frame this file should press: CCS is used politically as a permission slip — a producer state or an oil major can commit to net-zero without committing to less extraction, precisely because the models grant the technology in advance. Name who benefits from that assumption. This matters directly to the Gulf, where national climate plans lean on CCS harder than anyone's and where the storage geology is genuinely good but the volumes announced remain a rounding error against the exported barrels. It is a Q&A format — take the underlying evidence and the numbers, not the framing, and skip it as an explainer if the reporting carries no new data.

stories.label: Telegram back on Apple App Store after disappearing worldwide
stories.summary: Telegram vanished from Apple's App Store worldwide on Monday and came back without either company explaining why. Lead with the word 'worldwide' and with the silence, because together they are the finding: one company's listing decision removed a messaging app from every iPhone user on earth simultaneously, and the restoration is as unexplained as the removal. Teach the mechanism our reader lives inside: iOS permits no other distribution channel outside the EU's DMA jurisdiction, so an App Store delisting is not a store decision but a functional ban — a user cannot sideload, a new device cannot install, and an app that ships security fixes through the store stops shipping them. Android users were unaffected for exactly this reason, and that asymmetry is the whole lesson about which platform's users have a fallback. Establish the record: the removal and restoration timestamps, whether the listing is fully restored (the reporting says the return is incomplete — say in what respect), what Apple and Telegram have and have not said, whether any regulatory demand or a policy violation is documented, and Telegram's user count in the affected markets. Then the frame that makes this ours: Telegram is not a Western convenience app — it is core civic and commercial infrastructure across Iran, where it routes around blocking; Central Asia; Indonesia; and much of the Arab world, and it is the channel opposition movements and small traders actually use. A silent gatekeeping decision in Cupertino is a communications outage in Tashkent and Tehran, and neither the affected users nor their governments have any route of appeal. Do not speculate on cause; the absence of an explanation is the reportable fact. Four carriers including Anadolu and Free Malaysia Today, divergence 0.15 — regional coverage present, and note the Hindustan Times framing that attributes the removal to social-media rumour is unsourced.

stories.label: 'Own the Narrative': Leaked Flock Guide Shows How It Teaches Cops to Promote Its Tech
stories.summary: A leaked internal Flock guide instructs police departments on how to lobby their own elected officials on the surveillance company's behalf. Lead with the document, because it is the upgrade on yesterday's filing: this file ran a former Flock salesperson's account of what he was told to promise, and a leaked playbook is the same allegation in the company's own words. Advance the arc, do not restate it — the new fact is written instruction, so quote it. Teach the mechanism our reader should recognise in any procurement: the vendor cannot lobby a city council as effectively as the police chief can, because the chief is the council's own expert witness and appears as a neutral public servant — so the playbook converts a customer into an advocate and makes the body doing the oversight dependent on the entity being overseen for its information. That is the accountability gap, and it is structural rather than a matter of anyone lying. Establish the record: what the guide actually instructs (specific tactics, talking points, who it is addressed to), its provenance and how 404 obtained it, which departments have used it, what Flock says, and what the quoted critic's standing is. Then the frame: automatic licence-plate readers create a searchable national record of every vehicle's movements, and the councils approving them are being briefed by a party trained by the seller — a reader in any municipality can check whether their own department received this document. Note also where this travels: Flock and its competitors sell the same systems to Gulf and South Asian municipalities where there is no council to lobby at all, which removes the only friction the playbook was written to overcome. Second and final filing on this arc for now. Genuine document scoop from an investigative outlet — the single-source exception applies squarely.

stories.label: Did Iran hack water systems in seven US states?
stories.summary: Minnesota reported a co-ordinated cyber-attack on more than 30 of its water systems; days later the FBI said seven states were affected and that some activity 'degraded water operations'. Lead with the attribution question in the headline rather than answering it, because the honest finding is that the evidence for who did this is not public and the naming is happening anyway — during an active war with Iran, which is precisely when attribution is least reliable and most useful. Teach the mechanism our reader can carry: US water utilities are thousands of small municipal operators running industrial control systems that were never designed to face the internet, often reachable through a vendor's remote-maintenance link with a default password — so 'a state actor breached critical infrastructure' and 'someone scanned the internet for exposed PLCs' produce identical initial evidence, and the 2023 Aliquippa intrusion was exactly that. Distinguish 'degraded operations' from 'contaminated water', because they are not the same claim and only one has been made. Establish the record: what CISA and the FBI actually stated versus what officials characterised, which systems and what the degradation consisted of, what technical indicators have been published, Iran's response, and what independent researchers say about the attribution basis. Then the frame our reader should hold, and it cuts in a direction the coverage will not: attribution claims during wartime are a policy instrument — they justify response — so the standard of evidence matters most exactly when the political incentive to name is highest, and readers who have watched attribution used to license escalation in this region will want to know what is actually known. BBC doing verification rather than relaying; keep the interrogative honestly open if the evidence does not close it.
